_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Ringtones
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 26, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Tuesday. The server's down and an email's up: $800 a month for a banner ad for ringtones. The strip draws the offer as a phone ringing with a song it won't name. Wood answers it. The strip cuts before he says yes. Panel 1: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a dark garage with a CRT showing an error screen and a small flip phone ringing on the drafting table with music notes, a man and a small dog both staring at it (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, close-up of a flip phone screen showing a short dollar offer with music notes drawn like helicopter rotor lines rising off it. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a man's eyes moving between an eviction notice under a mug and a ringing phone with a thin drawn line connecting the two, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a man opening a flip phone in a dark garage with his mouth closed, a small dog lowering its head, no words (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_garage shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31; @loc_garage for the setting.
